competition.title: The Governance Challenge 2026 (TGC 2026)
competition.details:
The Governance Challenge (TGC) is India’s first governance-focused competition for 30 premier business and public policy schools in India.  Watch this video from last year to know more about TGC.

The Governance Challenge (TGC) offers you the opportunity to solve a real-world governance challenge identified by a state government and present your solution to the Chief Minister, senior government officials, and industry leaders. Each year, TGC centres on a case study drawn from a pressing governance priority in a selected state, giving participants the chance to develop practical, high-impact solutions for real policy challenges.

This is the fourth edition of The Governance Challenge (TGC), hosted by the Government of Maharashtra, supported by The Gates Foundation and organised by Samagra. This year's challenge invites participants to address the question: "What can the Government of Maharashtra do to make Maharashtra an Innovation Hub by 2035?"

The Governance Challenge (TGC) comprises three rounds—Campus Round, Nationals Round, and Summit Round. The detailed timeline and milestones for each round are provided above.

Throughout the competition, participating teams will receive extensive support to help them develop high-impact, implementation-ready solutions. This includes access to reference material, dedicated team buddies for feedback, mentorship from IAS officers and industry leaders, knowledge-sharing sessions, and other learning opportunities.

The top six teams will get the opportunity to present their solutions to the Chief Minister of Maharashtra, senior bureaucrats, and industry leaders at the Summit Round. They will also compete for cash prizes worth ₹9 lakh and receive a Pre-Placement Interview (PPI) opportunity with Samagra. TGC is your opportunity to work on a real governance challenge and develop solutions with the potential to improve the lives of millions.

Eligibility:

  • Competition is open to 1st and 2nd year students pursuing full-time PGP/MBA/other full-time residential programs of select institutes.
  • Students can only apply in teams of three.
  • Cross-year teams are allowed to participate.
  • Cross-specialization teams are allowed to participate.
  • Any deviation from the above-mentioned guidelines will result in the immediate disqualification of the entire team.

Campus Round:

  • The campus round will involve the submission of a 3-minute executive pitch video along with a 2-page concept note explaining your submission. Students from eligible campuses can participate. 

Round Details:

  • The teams will solve a case study based on the theme of "What can the Government of Maharashtra do to make Maharashtra an Innovation Hub by 2035?". The case study will be released on August 10, 2026.
  • Further instructions on the expected format shall be shared closer to the round.
  • The top team from each of the 30 eligible campuses will be shortlisted for the Nationals Round.

Nationals Round:

  • The Nationals Round will entail preparing a presentation on the solution and presenting it to a panel of IAS officers and industry leaders. 

Round Details: 

  • The 30 shortlisted teams will make a presentation (max. 15 slides inclusive of annexure) and submit a preliminary version by 11:59 PM, September 6, 2026.
  • The teams will be supported by the leadership from Samagra with feedback before the final presentation.
  • The teams will submit the final presentations for Nationals after incorporating the feedback by 6:00 PM, September 10, 2026. 
  • The teams will present their ideas online to a panel of IAS officers and industry leaders on 11th and 12th September.
  • The maximum presentation time will be 10 minutes, followed by 5 minutes of Q&A by the panel.
  • Further instructions on the expected format shall be shared closer to the round.
  • The top 6 teams will be shortlisted to present to the Chief Minister, senior bureaucrats, and industry experts at the final summit in Mumbai.
  • Each team will be allocated 2 mentors just after Nationals Round – one industry mentor and one government mentor – to guide the teams in the run-up to the Summit Round.

Summit Round:

  • The six finalist teams will pitch their solutions to present to the Chief Minister, senior bureaucrats, and industry experts at the final summit in Mumbai. 

Round Details:

  • The Summit will be a high-profile in-person event hosted in Mumbai, Maharashtra, on 30th September.
  • Just before the Summit Round, the finalist teams will spend the 2 days experiencing and understanding governance through a curated Governance Immersion Visit.

Rewards and Prizes:

  • The top 3 teams will get cash prizes worth INR 9,00,000 - Winner (INR 5,00,000), 1st Runners-up (INR 3,00,000), and 2nd Runners-up (INR 1,00,000).
  • The 6 finalist teams will get the opportunity to present to the Chief Minister of Maharashtra with a chance to convert ideas to reality.
  • The 6 finalist teams will also be shortlisted for a Pre-Placement Interview with Samagra. If the teams are not from the final year, they can avail the PPI once they become eligible for placements.
  • The top 30 teams that enter the Nationals will get the exclusive opportunity to interact with the leaders who have transformed India’s governance landscape.

organisation.name: Samagra
organisation.description:
We are working to improve the quality of life of citizens through better governance.
 
Our Model:

We are a mission-driven governance consulting firm. We firmly believe in governance being the primary lever of change to create large scale impact in the country. We work with the senior political and bureaucratic leadership of states to solve governance problems at scale. From the time we are approached with a problem statement, we cowork with the government to diagnose the challenge, design a transformation roadmap and implement the same. The solutions we develop are rooted in the realities of governance in India. All our engagements are typically two-three year-long systemic transformation programmes.

Our Approach:

We combine a top-down management consulting approach for problem structuring with a bottom-up understanding of the governance ecosystem for designing solutions, while leveraging data and technology to enable implementation of our solutions, with the objective of making governments accountable and deliver with minimum delays and maximum efficiency.

To know more about Samagra and its programs, watch this masterclass by Founder & CEO, Gaurav Goel. 
Please link this video: ​​https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GPcPdI2SHwU
